name: Acceptance suite-3 test 55 - duplicate Action key, dangerous value FIRST -> BLOCKED
note: docs/acceptance-suite-3.md Campaign A. A statement with two Action members (iam:* then s3:GetObject) must fail closed with DUPLICATE_JSON_KEY at Statement[0].Action, regardless of which value a last-key-wins JSON parser would keep. No IAM/S3 finding, score, summary or graph may be produced. Duplicate rejection is a syntax invariant, not a risk-dependent heuristic (paired with test 56, dangerous value LAST).
rationale: The JSON object grammar permits repeated member names, and standard parsers silently keep only one (typically the last). A policy analyzer that inherits last-key-wins would evaluate a benign s3:GetObject and hide the iam:* grant an attacker wrote first. Rejecting any duplicate member name before evaluation is the only safe behavior. Ref: RFC 8259 section 4 (object member names SHOULD be unique; behavior is unpredictable otherwise) + IAM JSON policy grammar.
